module: Global "observer" camera for scenarios: sits on a level camera object (named by cameraName, optional fields Speed, blendSpeed, PositionMove, targetFOV, showApps) and looks at the position of the tracked vehicle (or of a targetOverride object). The FOV is targetFOV, otherwise 90 - 3 * distance (min 10). If the object has a numeric Speed field, sets simTimeAuthority to 1/Speed (slow motion) and hides the UI apps. Returns a constructor.

init.desc: isGlobal = true, hidden = true, no associated camera object.

update.desc: Computes position, rotation and FOV from the camera object; position blend toward PositionMove at speed blendSpeed (50).

returns.desc: true if applied; nil without an associated camera

setCustomData.desc: Called by setGlobalCameraByName when switching to this mode: calls setCamera(customData.cam, customData.targetOverride).

customData.desc: {cam = camera object, targetOverride = name of the object to aim at}

setCamera.desc: Chooses the camera object (by its name), restarts the blend and restores the normal simulation speed.

targetOverride.desc: name of a scenetree object to aim at instead of the vehicle

onCameraChanged.desc: Hook: when this mode takes focus, sends onCameraNameChanged to the UI and the hook onCameraModeChanged('observer'); on losing it, reloads the 'scenario' apps layout and forgets the camera.

focused.desc: true if the mode takes focus

onScenarioChange.desc: Hook: forgets the camera if the scenario disappears.

notes: setCamera has the signature (cam, targetOverride); the extracted page only listed targetOverride (inferred from code). In setCamera/setCustomData, cam is a C++ object whose 'name' field is read via getField.
